candidate_long_name: pit_round2-derived joint (RULING-C1 composition of pre-registered candidate #1)
ceiling_statement: Per Grok WO-7 section 2 (correcting RULING-C1 section 3.5): the four solo deltas sum to 0.041164 against a gate distance of 0.055021 (7.154021 - 7.099). That sum is an optimistic illustration under perfect additivity, NOT an upper bound. Sub-additivity is the default expectation (F2/F3 share mechanism), super-additivity is possible in principle only via a lattice x key-number-atom interaction for which no evidence exists, and prior stack tests moved the other way. Realistic compositions are expected to land short of even the additive approx-7.113 figure.

composition.excess_mass: F2's landed key-number atoms on absolute margins {-7,-3,+3,+7} (pit_round2.keynum_components)
composition.kernel: Student-t, variance-matched: s = sigma*sqrt((nu-2)/nu); nu = inf -> Gaussian
composition.mean_lock: exact: c_g is the unique root of sum_k k*P_g(k) = mu_g (bisection)

fit_performance_note: The ruled procedure (exact mean-lock bisection inside every objective evaluation of a joint CRPS fit over the full point-in-time training set) is compute-heavy in pure Python: measured 2026-10-15, one objective evaluation over 30 synthetic rows took ~1.7s before tail-stable vectorisation, and the synthetic test suite exercises the fit on reduced row counts / nu subsets for runtime. A production weekly fit at full training-set scale needs a performance pass (batched pmf construction) before FREEZE-1; the mathematics is unchanged by that pass. Flagged, not silently optimised, because the bisection method is named in the ruling.

P2.detail: Landed F2 code exposes its mechanisms as callable pieces; NO refactor was needed. sigma: pit_round2.hetero_sd(beta_T, total_line) (functional form sigma0*exp(clip(beta_T*(total/44), -0.45, 0.45))). Atom set/weights: pit_round2.keynum_components(mu, sd, p3, p7) -> (w, c, atoms) with atoms {(+3,p3/2),(-3,p3/2),(+7,p7/2),(-7,p7/2)} on absolute margins. theta_sigma = beta_T (grid BETA_GRID -0.20..0.20), theta_A = (p3, p7) (grid P_GRID). prj1 imports both rather than re-deriving them, so the frozen candidate cannot drift from the landed structure; synthetic pins assert prj1.sigma_g == pit_round2.hetero_sd and atom placement/weights to 1e-12.

P3.detail: Every covariate F2's sigma/atom mechanisms consume, vs archiver availability at T_emit. COMPLETE covariate list: (1) total_line -- consumed by hetero_sd as xT = total_line/44; ARCHIVER-AVAILABLE at T_emit (the line archiver's stamped spread/total/moneyline captures; SPEC-A mu = archived line at T_emit). (2) mu = spread_line at T_emit -- this is the prediction input itself, archiver-stamped by SPEC-A construction. Atom mechanism consumes NO covariates (fixed absolute set {-7,-3,+3,+7}; weights are fitted parameters). GAPS: none for the ruled mechanisms. Two notes, reported not papered over: (a) hetero_sd's landed fallback substitutes total_line = 44.0 when the total is missing (fail-soft inside the landed code; retained as-is because the candidate inherits F2's mechanism verbatim); (b) atom weights are week-level fitted parameters, so their point-in-time availability is governed by the section 1.4 refit rule, not by the archiver.
P3.status: SATISFIED (one covariate; no gaps; two notes)

P4.detail: The evaluator's CRPS handles integer-support pmfs exactly, verified in code: pit_round2.crps_discrete integrates (F(u) - 1{u>=y})^2 du exactly for a step-function F on consecutive integers (segment-wise, split at y, exact left-tail term) -- no binning approximation. It is the function F1 was scored with. prj1's fitting objective and crps_pmf use it imported, not re-derived; test pins its exactness on degenerate pmfs (|2 - y|) to 1e-12.
